- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 3–7 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price shows mean reversion, model often fails to adjust; use 3-period moving average to anchor forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.27) and price is volatile, model overfits recent noise; use 5-day smoothing to reduce false peaks.
